BOTH CLEAN, 0 issues opened. #2956 (react-web, ppt-web, 28/-15, 1 file): precisely closes #2954's two low findings on queryKeys.test.ts -- (a) suite-crash risk fixed by a new non-throwing displayRoot() feeding only the it.each case title while rootOf()'s throwing shape-assertion moved INSIDE each it() callback (a malformed factory now fails its own named row instead of aborting suite collection), applied consistently to all three it.each blocks (central/feature-local/api-client); (b) glob-depth widened '../features/**/hooks/*.{ts,tsx}' -> '**/hooks/**/*' with the {test,spec} exclusion widened in lock-step so a factory nested under hooks/ can't escape discovery. Verify OK (biome+typecheck+136 files/2666 tests green). Minimal, exactly-scoped, no scope drift. #2955 (react-native, mobile, 147/-2, 4 files): precisely closes #2953's high security finding -- resetLocalData() now purges the actual NFC building-access credential material that its AsyncStorage sweep never reached. New static NFCCredentialManager.clearAllLocalCredentials() deletes the encrypted SecureStore manifest+chunk slots (extracted to a shared private static deleteStoredCredentials(), reused by the existing instance clearStoredCredentials() -> no duplication) AND removes the legacy unencrypted AsyncStorage blob (LEGACY_CREDENTIALS_KEY='@ppt/nfc_credentials'); called from resetLocalData() in its OWN best-effort try/catch AFTER the AsyncStorage sweep so a sweep failure can't skip the more sensitive purge. Verified against source: chunk sweep bound MAX_CREDENTIAL_CHUNKS=64 matches the write path (not a new gap); resetLocalData IS the real session-change purge point (wired into AuthContext login L123 + logout L159), so the static purge actually runs on handoff -- both keys the prior review flagged are now covered. Strong regression tests (direct clearAll unit test + two resetLocalData tests: both surfaces purged while unrelated SecureStore auth token survives, and purge still runs when the AsyncStorage sweep throws); biome+typecheck green, jest unrunnable in-runner due to pre-existing jest-expo<->RN0.87 rot (#2951, repo-wide, not this PR). Residual out-of-scope note (NOT filed): a long-lived in-memory NFCCredentialManager instance's this.credentials array is not nulled by the static purge -- but #2953 was scoped to persisted material and the manager is session-scoped, so no live bug. with_issues.note: gh-issue-2947 fix purges @ppt/access_log, @ppt/qr_scan_history, @ppt/feedback_drafts, @ppt/pending_feedback, @ppt/faq_votes via new TENANT_SCOPED_EXACT_KEYS registry in resetLocalData() -- correct and well-tested for what it covers. 1 finding, security(high): auditing the same NFCCredentialManager.ts this PR references turned up two still-uncovered, MORE sensitive keys neither resetLocalData() nor AuthContext.login()/logout() touch: (1) LEGACY_CREDENTIALS_KEY='@ppt/nfc_credentials' (raw unencrypted legacy credential blob in AsyncStorage, not in TENANT_SCOPED_EXACT_KEYS) -- if migration hasn't run yet this session, the prior tenant's blob survives resetLocalData() and the next tenant's loadStoredCredentials() silently adopts it as its own; (2) CREDENTIALS_KEY='ppt_nfc_credentials'+chunk slots in expo-secure-store (written by storeCredentials()) are never cleared on session change at all -- resetLocalData() only touches AsyncStorage. Between logout and the next tenant's first fetchCredentials(), the prior tenant's actual NFC building-access credential material (not just the log) remains loadable -- same shared-device leak class this PR fixed for the log, but for the credential itself. Proposed: expose NFCCredentialManager.clearAllLocalCredentials() (wrapping the existing private clearStoredCredentials() + AsyncStorage.removeItem(LEGACY_CREDENTIALS_KEY)) and call it from resetLocalData() or alongside it in AuthContext login/logout; add a regression test mirroring resetLocalData.test.ts's new it.each block. Filed #2953.

gh-issue-2948 generalizes queryKeys.test.ts to auto-discover feature-local *Keys factories via import.meta.glob('../features/**/hooks/*.{ts,tsx}',{eager:true}) instead of a hand-maintained import list -- correct fix for the 'reviewer must remember' gap, incidentally also now covers messagingKeys which the old hardcoded list missed. 2 low findings: (1) test-gaps -- rootOf(name,factory)'s shape assertions run inside the it.each-table-building .map(), i.e. at describe-evaluation time not inside an it() callback, so a malformed factory would throw during suite collection and abort the WHOLE file's tests instead of failing just its own named row; proposed moving the assertion inside the it.each callback. (2) correctness -- the glob '../features/**/hooks/*.{ts,tsx}' only matches files directly under a hooks/ dir (trailing single '*', not '**'), so a factory in a nested features/<x>/hooks/queries/<y>.ts would silently escape discovery again -- no such nested layout exists today (latent, not live) but is exactly the failure mode this PR closes; proposed widening to 'hooks/**/*.{ts,tsx}'. Filed #2954.
